title: A reply that breaks clause 5 is replaced by an error message that still carries the echo

provenance.quote: If any NLIP message containing a submessage that where the format field is 'token', the end-point must include the same submessage with the exact same format, subformat and content in its response message to the peer end-point, except when the token was initially created by the end-point.

notes: The handler returned a `text` message whose content is an object, which §5.1.4 does not allow — the message-level case is `readings/12`. A malformed reply is worse for the peer than an error reply, because the peer has to guess what was meant, so the reply is replaced by a protocol-legal one and the finding is handed back for the runtime to log. Two readings are recorded here. The replacement's `MessageType: Error` is TR/113 §10's convention rather than a rule of clause 5. And the replacement happens *before* the echo, not after, so `cli-1` is in the reply: the peer's entitlement under §6.2 does not depend on the end-point's handler having worked, and an implementation that sanitised last would drop it on exactly the path where a peer most needs its state back. `withheld` is the third thing, and it is not derivable from the reply: a replacement error message and a handler that answered with `Message::error(..)` are the same bytes on the wire, and a binding reading only those bytes would report the end-point's failure as a success. `ecma-430/30` pins the other value.
